p.text: What does Kamola tell Aziz to do with numbers and percentages?
options: Give the count only when the rise is a large one
Give both, or give the one that does not mislead
Always give the percentage and leave the count out
Give whichever of the two the reader is expecting

fb.correct: 'Give both, always, or give the one that does not mislead.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'Give both, always, or give the one that does not mislead.'

1.say: The editor wants a second voice in the piece. There is only one side. The figures are not disputed by anybody. Then giving the other side half the page tells the reader the question is open when it is not. She will say it is fair. It is fair to two writers and unfair to every reader. Balance is a tool for questions that are actually open, not a rule. There is a line I want to keep. 'Cases doubled in a month.' From what to what? From two to four. Then it is true and it is a lie. Give the numbers and let the reader see how small they are. So the percentage is the dishonest form. Sometimes it is the honest one. A rise of a hundred per cent from two cases means nothing at all. Give both, always, or give the one that does not mislead.

key: The editor wants a second voice in the piece.

grammar.label: the false balance and the question that is not open
grammar.form: presenting two positions as equally supported when the evidence is not equal
grammar.meaning: creates an appearance of controversy by the shape of the sentence

explanation.en: 'Some say the road is safe; others disagree' gives two clauses of equal weight to a question where one side has the engineering report. Grammatical symmetry implies evidential symmetry, and readers take the implication. The fix is asymmetric wording, not the removal of the second view.
explanation.uz: 'Some say the road is safe; others disagree' — muhandislik hisoboti bir tomonda bo'lsa ham, ikki gap teng og'irlikda. Grammatik simmetriya dalil simmetriyasini anglatadi.

grammar.positive_example: The engineers say it is unsafe; two councillors, who have not read the report, disagree.
grammar.negative_example: Some say the bridge is unsafe, while others take a different view.

l1_notes.uz: Ikki tomonni teng ko'rsatish adolatli tuyuladi, lekin dalil teng bo'lmasa, aslida chalg'itadi.

grammar.label: statistics in prose — the sentence that misleads while telling the truth
grammar.form: percentages without bases; relative risk without absolute; averages hiding distributions
grammar.meaning: states a true number in a frame that produces a false impression

explanation.en: 'Cases doubled' is true if they went from one to two. 'The average household gained' is true when nine lost and one gained enormously. Nothing here is a lie, and every one of them misleads. At C2 the reading skill is to ask, of each number, what the sentence is not telling you.
explanation.uz: 'Cases doubled' — birdan ikkiga chiqqan bo'lsa ham rost. 'O'rtacha xonadon yutdi' — to'qqiztasi yo'qotib, bittasi ko'p yutgan bo'lsa ham rost. Hech biri yolg'on emas, hammasi chalg'itadi.

grammar.positive_example: Cases rose from one to two; the paper reported that they had doubled.
grammar.negative_example: Cases doubled this month, which shows the scale of the problem.

l1_notes.uz: Statistik jumlalar rost bo'lib ham chalg'itishi mumkin; bu ko'p ta'lim tizimida o'rgatilmaydi.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The editor wants a second voice in the piece.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is only one side. The figures are not disputed by anybody.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then giving the other side half the page tells the reader the question is open when it is not.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She will say it is fair.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is fair to two writers and unfair to every reader. Balance is a tool for questions that are actually open, not a rule.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is a line I want to keep. 'Cases doubled in a month.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then it is true and it is a lie. Give the numbers and let the reader see how small they are.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So the percentage is the dishonest form.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sometimes it is the honest one. A rise of a hundred per cent from two cases means nothing at all. Give both, always, or give the one that does not mislead.
